stories.text: Nadia kept bees behind the chapel. One summer a bear broke the fence and knocked over two hives. Her neighbour Osip helped her mend the fence with old planks. In return Nadia gave him a pot of honey every month until winter.

The ferryman rowed people across the river for a penny. One foggy evening a doctor begged him to cross without paying. The ferryman agreed because the doctor's patient was a child. The next morning the doctor left a silver spoon on the ferryman's bench.
qs: Who begged to cross without paying?
When did the doctor leave it?

stories.text: Two sisters, Ilse and Greta, shared a garden. Ilse grew cabbages and Greta grew roses. When hail flattened the cabbages, Greta sold her roses at the market and bought seed for Ilse. By autumn the cabbages were bigger than before.
qs: Who sold roses at the market?

stories.text: Old Benedek owned the only clock in the village. Every noon he rang a bell so the farmers knew the hour. One day the clock stopped, and the farmers ate lunch late. A travelling tinker named Jules fixed the clock for a bowl of soup.
qs: What did Benedek do every noon?
What happened when the clock stopped?
What did Jules get for fixing it?

stories.text: A fox and a stork were invited to dinner by the badger. The badger served soup in flat dishes, which the stork could not eat. The stork said nothing and went home hungry. A week later the stork served dinner in tall jars, and the fox went home hungry.
qs: Who invited the fox and the stork?
What was served in flat dishes?
What did the stork serve dinner in?
Who went home hungry a week later?

stories.text: Captain Mireille sailed a cargo of salt to the northern port. A storm tore the sail, and the cook, Pavel, sewed it with fishing line. They arrived three days late. The merchant paid them anyway because the salt was dry.
qs: What cargo did the ship carry?
What did Pavel sew it with?
Why did the merchant pay them?

stories.text: Tomasz the baker hired a boy named Rafal to sweep the floor. Rafal found a gold ring under the oven and gave it to Tomasz. The ring belonged to Tomasz's late wife. Tomasz taught Rafal to bake and later left him the shop.
qs: Who was hired to sweep the floor?

stories.text: The schoolmistress, Miss Abena, walked to the next village every Thursday to teach reading. In the rainy season the path flooded, so the children's fathers built her a footbridge of logs. She named the bridge after the oldest pupil, Kofi.
qs: On which day did Miss Abena walk to the next village?
What was the bridge made of?
Who was the bridge named after?

stories.text: A miller's donkey refused to climb the hill with a sack of flour. The miller's daughter, Lucia, put an apple on a string in front of its nose. The donkey walked all the way to the top. At the top Lucia gave it the apple and a second one.
qs: What did the donkey refuse to do?
Who put an apple on a string?
How many apples did the donkey get at the top?

stories.text: Every winter the lake near Varde froze, and the children skated on it. One year a boy named Erlend fell through thin ice near the reeds. A fisherman called Sven pulled him out with a ladder. After that the mayor had the reeds marked with red flags.
qs: What did the children do on the lake?
What did the mayor have marked?

stories.text: A wolf saw a lamb drinking at a stream. The wolf said the lamb was muddying his water. The lamb replied that it stood downstream. The wolf ate the lamb anyway.
qs: Who was drinking at the stream?
What did the wolf say the lamb was doing?

stories.text: An ant worked all summer storing grain. A grasshopper sang in the sun and laughed at her. When winter came, the grasshopper begged the ant for food. The ant gave him a single seed and shut her door.
qs: What did the ant give the grasshopper?

stories.text: "Give me the lantern," said Marta. Her brother Piet handed it over without a word. They walked to the cellar together. Marta found the missing cat behind a barrel and carried it upstairs.
The mouse gnawed through the net and freed the lion. The lion had laughed at the mouse a week before. Now the lion bowed his head and thanked the mouse. The hunters found an empty net at dawn.
qs: What did the mouse gnaw through?
Who had laughed at the mouse?

stories.text: "Is the bridge safe?" asked the traveller. The miller shook his head. "The flood took the middle plank," he said. The traveller crossed by the ford instead and reached the inn by nightfall.
qs: Where did the traveller reach by nightfall?

stories.text: A crow stole a ring from the goldsmith's bench. The goldsmith's daughter, Ines, followed the crow to the church tower. She climbed the tower and found a nest full of rings. Ines returned every ring to the village.
qs: Where did the crow take the ring?
What did Ines find in the tower?
What did Ines return to the village?

stories.text: Jack walked from the farm to the river. He slipped and fell in the mud. Jane met him by the river and laughed. Jack washed his coat and then they walked to the mill together.
qs: Where was Jack at the end?
Who was with Jack at the mill?

stories.text: Mira had a red boat. Tomas took the boat to the island. He left the boat on the beach there and walked to the lighthouse. Mira rowed the spare boat to the island and found the red boat on the beach.
qs: Where was the red boat at the end?
Where was Tomas at the end?
Who had the red boat first?
Where did Mira find the red boat?
Who took the boat to the island?

stories.text: The baker gave Petra a roll. Petra gave the roll to her brother Ivo. Ivo ate half and put the other half in his pocket. Later a dog stole the half from Ivo's pocket.
qs: Who had the roll after Petra?
Where was the half roll before the dog took it?
Who had the half roll at the end?
What did Ivo do with the first half?

stories.text: Three riders raced to the bridge. Olaf reached the bridge first. Beth arrived second, and Kemal came last because his horse lost a shoe. Beth then rode on to the village while Olaf waited at the bridge.
qs: Where was Beth at the end?
Where was Olaf at the end?

stories.text: In the morning the key was on the hook. At noon Rosa took the key to the garden. She dropped it near the well. In the evening Felix found the key and hung it back on the hook.
qs: Where was the key at noon?
Where was the key in the evening?
Where did Rosa drop the key?
Where was the key in the morning?

stories.text: Nils carried a lantern into the cave. He set the lantern down at the fork and went left. He came back without finding anything, picked up the lantern, and went right. At the end of the right tunnel he found a chest.
qs: Where did Nils leave the lantern?
Which way did Nils go first?
Where did Nils find the chest?
the end of the right tunnel
Did Nils have the lantern when he found the chest?
Where was Nils at the end?
the end of the right tunnel

stories.text: Halvard repaired bicycles in a shed beside the railway station. On Monday a schoolgirl, Keiko, brought him a wheel with a broken spoke. He fixed it while she waited, but he would not take her money. Instead Keiko painted a new sign for his shed, and customers began to notice it from the platform.
qs: What did Halvard refuse to take?
Who brought a wheel with a broken spoke?
When did Keiko bring the wheel?

stories.text: A magpie lived above a pond where a vain frog sang every night. The frog boasted that his voice could call down the moon. One evening the magpie dropped a shiny button into the water, and the frog, thinking it was the moon, dived after it. He never found it, and from then on he sang more quietly.
qs: What did the magpie do one evening?
What did the frog think the button was?
How did the frog sing afterwards?

stories.text: At seven o'clock the umbrella hung by Farida's front door. She took it on the bus to her office, where she left it in the kitchen. At lunchtime her colleague Bruno borrowed the umbrella to fetch sandwiches. He came back soaked, because he had left it at the bakery.
qs: Where was the umbrella at seven o'clock?
Where did Farida leave the umbrella at her office?
Where was the umbrella at the end?

stories.text: Mrs. Adeyemi ran the corner shop on Linden Street. Her nephew Tobias, who was saving for a guitar, stacked the shelves every Saturday. One Saturday a pipe burst in the storeroom and flooded the boxes of rice. Tobias carried the boxes into the yard to dry, and Mrs. Adeyemi paid him double that week.
qs: What flooded the boxes of rice?
Where did Tobias carry the boxes?
How much did Mrs. Adeyemi pay him that week?

stories.text: A goat and a donkey shared a field behind a monastery. The goat was jealous because the monks fed the donkey oats. He told the donkey to pretend to be lame so that it could rest all day. The monks called a vet, who gave the donkey a bitter medicine, and the donkey never listened to the goat again.
qs: What did the monks feed the donkey?
Who gave the donkey a bitter medicine?
What did the goat tell the donkey to do?

stories.text: Grandpa Emeka left his glasses on the porch after breakfast. Around ten, his granddaughter Zuri carried them inside and put them on the piano. In the afternoon the piano tuner moved them to the windowsill so that he could open the lid. That evening Emeka searched the porch for an hour before Zuri remembered.
qs: Where were the glasses after breakfast?
Where were the glasses at noon?
Who moved the glasses to the windowsill?
Where were the glasses at the end?

stories.text: Dr. Lindqvist was the only dentist on the island, so patients came to her by boat. One stormy week no boats could cross, and a fisherman named Kwame had a terrible toothache. She borrowed the harbour master's radio and talked Kwame through the worst night. When the sea calmed, he arrived with a basket of crabs as a thank-you.
qs: Who was the only dentist on the island?
Whose radio did the dentist borrow?
When did Kwame bring the crabs?

stories.text: An owl kept the keys to the forest library, where the squirrels hid acorns between the pages. One autumn a careless squirrel, Pip, chewed a whole book of maps. The owl made him copy every map by hand onto birch bark. It took Pip until the first snow, and by then he knew the name of every river.
qs: Who kept the keys to the library?
Who chewed the book of maps?
What did the squirrels hide between the pages?
What did Pip copy the maps onto?

stories.text: Ximena and her father drove from the city to the coast on Friday. They stopped at a farm stall for strawberries and reached the beach hut by sunset. On Saturday Ximena swam out to the buoy while her father fished from the pier. On Sunday they drove home with a cooler full of mackerel.
qs: Where were they at sunset on Friday?
Where was Ximena's father on Saturday?
Who swam out to the buoy?

stories.text: The night guard at the museum, Mr. Haddad, heard a crash in the Egyptian room. A cat had knocked a clay jar off its stand, but the jar landed on a cushion and did not break. Mr. Haddad carried the cat outside and wrote a report. The next day the curator moved every jar behind glass.
qs: What knocked the jar off its stand?
What did the jar land on?
What did the curator do the next day?

stories.text: A proud peacock refused to share the shade of the fig tree with a dusty sparrow. At midday a hawk circled overhead, and the peacock's bright tail shone in the sun. The sparrow shrieked a warning, and the peacock hid just in time. After that, the peacock let the sparrow sit beside him.
qs: Who refused to share the shade?

stories.text: On Tuesday morning the parcel left the warehouse in Ghent on a lorry. By the afternoon it had been sorted at the depot in Lille. Agnieszka, the Wednesday driver, took it to the village post office because nobody was home at the address. On Thursday morning Mr. Ferreira collected it there and carried it to his flat.
qs: Where was the parcel on Tuesday morning?
What carried the parcel from Ghent?
Who took the parcel to the post office?
Where was the parcel at the end?

stories.text: Every spring the twins, Arjun and Meera, helped their aunt plant rice in the paddy below her house. This year Arjun sprained his ankle on the first day. Meera planted his rows as well as her own, while Arjun sat on the bank and counted the seedlings. When the planting was done, their aunt cooked a feast for both of them.
qs: What did the twins help plant?

stories.text: A camel and a rooster crossed the desert with a caravan. The rooster complained that the sand burned his feet, so the camel let him ride on its hump. In return, the rooster woke the traders each dawn. When a sandstorm came, the camel knelt and the rooster hid under its neck.
qs: When did the rooster wake them?
What did the camel do when the sandstorm came?

stories.text: Before school, Yusuf put his football in his bag. At break he lent it to his friend Dario, who kicked it over the fence into Mrs. Kowalczyk's garden. She kept the ball in her shed until the bell rang at three. Then Yusuf knocked on her door, apologized, and took the ball home.
qs: What did Yusuf put in his bag?
Who kicked the ball over the fence?
Whose garden did the ball land in?
Where did Mrs. Kowalczyk keep the ball?
Who had the ball at the end?

stories.text: A young reporter, Sione, was sent to cover the town's pumpkin show. The biggest pumpkin belonged to a retired teacher, who had grown it in a bathtub. While Sione was taking photographs, the table under the pumpkin cracked. Six farmers lifted it onto a cart, and Sione's picture of them made the front page.
qs: Who was sent to the pumpkin show?
Where had the pumpkin been grown?
How many farmers lifted the pumpkin?

stories.text: A hedgehog borrowed a lantern from a mole so she could find her way home after dark. On the path she met a lost rabbit kit crying for its mother. The hedgehog gave the kit the lantern and walked home in the dark herself. The next day the rabbits brought the mole a new lantern and the hedgehog a basket of clover.
qs: Who lent the hedgehog a lantern?
Who was crying for its mother?
Who had the lantern after the hedgehog met the kit?
What did the rabbits bring the hedgehog?
What did the rabbits bring the mole?

stories.text: The museum's painting of a lighthouse was taken down on Monday for cleaning. It spent the week in the restorer's workshop on the top floor. On Saturday two porters carried it to the east gallery, but it was too wide for the wall there. By Sunday evening it was back in its old place in the hall.
qs: When was the painting taken down?
Where was the painting during the week?
Who carried the painting to the east gallery?
Why did the painting not stay in the east gallery?
Where was the painting on Sunday evening?

stories.text: When the bakery's oven broke, its owner, Chiara, asked the pizza shop next door for help. The pizza maker, Mehmet, let her bake bread in his oven before he opened at eleven. For a week the whole street smelled of bread and pizza at once. Chiara repaid him with a cake shaped like a pizza.
qs: Who let Chiara use his oven?
a cake shaped like a pizza

stories.text: A young elephant wanted to cross the river, but the crocodile told him the water was too deep. The elephant's grandmother laughed and walked straight in. The water only came up to her knees, and the crocodile slid away, ashamed of his lie. That day the young elephant learned that a crocodile's advice is not always kind.
qs: Who said the water was too deep?
Who walked straight into the river?
Why did the crocodile slide away?
What did the young elephant want to cross?

stories.text: In the morning the fishing boat lay in the harbour at Skerry. By noon its skipper, Oona, had taken it out to the reef. A gale pushed the boat north, so she sheltered in a cove for the night. The next day she sailed back to Skerry with an empty hold.
qs: Where was the boat in the morning?
Where was the boat at noon?
What did Oona sail back with?

stories.text: Mr. Varga, who drove the school bus, noticed that one boy always sat alone at the back. On Monday he asked the boy, Elias, to help him count the children at each stop. Soon the other children were asking Elias for the numbers. By Friday he was sitting in the middle of the bus with three new friends.
qs: When did Mr. Varga ask Elias to help?
What did Mr. Varga ask Elias to do?
Where did Elias sit by Friday?
How many new friends did Elias have?

stories.text: A beaver built a dam that flooded a heron's favourite fishing spot. The heron took his complaint to the old turtle, who judged the quarrels of the marsh. The turtle ruled that the beaver must leave a gap in the dam for the fish to pass. Now the heron fishes by the gap, and the beaver keeps his pond.
qs: What did the beaver's dam flood?
What must the beaver leave in the dam?
Where does the heron fish now?

stories.text: Kenji borrowed his brother's camera on Saturday morning and took it to the zoo. At the penguin pool he set it on a bench to eat lunch, and a keeper found it there an hour later. The keeper took the camera to the lost-property office by the gate. Kenji's brother, Hiro, collected it on Sunday.
qs: Where was the camera on Saturday night?

stories.text: The librarian, Ms. Osei, noticed that the same book about volcanoes came back late every month. She found out that a girl named Daria read it aloud to her grandfather, who could no longer see well. Ms. Osei ordered a large-print copy for him. Now Daria's grandfather reads the book on his own.
qs: What did Daria do with the book?

stories.text: A spider spun her web across the door of the barn. The farmer's broom swept it away every morning, and every night she spun it again. One summer the barn filled with flies, so the farmer stopped sweeping. The spider ate well, and the cows were grateful.
qs: Where did the spider spin her web?
across the door of the barn
When did the spider spin it again?

stories.text: At dawn the sheep were in the fold behind Aurelio's cottage. He drove them up to the high meadow by mid-morning. While he napped under an oak, his dog, Lupa, kept them away from the cliff edge. At dusk Aurelio and Lupa brought the flock down to the fold again.
qs: Where were the sheep at dawn?
When did Aurelio bring the flock down?
Who kept the sheep away from the cliff edge?
What did Aurelio do under the oak?

stories.text: Ingrid was a mechanic at the garage on the ring road. One morning a nervous young driver, Tariq, brought in a car that made a rattling noise. Ingrid opened the boot and found a tin of marbles rolling around. She handed the tin back with a smile and did not charge him anything.
qs: What was rolling around in the boot?
What did Ingrid do with the tin?
How much did Ingrid charge Tariq?

stories.text: A lazy cat promised the mice that she would never hunt again if they brought her one fish each week. The mice agreed and stole a fish from the market every Friday. One Friday the fishmonger's dog chased them home, and the cat, who had grown fat, could not even scare it away. The mice decided she was no longer worth paying.
qs: Who made a promise to the mice?
What did the cat ask for?
Where did the mice steal the fish?
When did the mice steal fish?

stories.text: Sana packed a picnic and cycled from her flat to the lake. She ate on the jetty, then left her bicycle against a pine and walked around the shore. A ranger moved the bicycle to the car park because it was blocking the path. Sana found it there an hour later and rode back to her flat.
qs: Where did Sana leave her bicycle?
Where was the bicycle when Sana found it?
Where was Sana at the end?

stories.text: Uncle Bartholomew had promised to bring the cake to the wedding, but he left it on the train. The station master telephoned the next town, where a porter found the cake on a luggage rack. A taxi driver brought it back just as the speeches began. The bride said it was the most travelled cake she had ever eaten.
qs: Who left the cake on the train?
When did the cake arrive back?

stories.text: A young wolf boasted that he could outrun the wind. The wind heard him and blew so hard that the wolf's ears lay flat. He ran until he collapsed by a well, and an old badger brought him water. "The wind never tires," said the badger, "but wolves do."
qs: What did the wolf say he could outrun?

stories.text: On the first day of the trip, Professor Mbeki's class took the train from Durban to the mountains. They spent the second day at a research hut beside a waterfall. On the third day a landslide closed the road, so a helicopter flew the students back to Durban. Professor Mbeki stayed behind with the equipment.
qs: Where were the students on the second day?
Where were the students at the end?

stories.text: The new postwoman, Rosalind, was bitten on the ankle by a terrier on her first day. The terrier's owner, a florist, felt so bad that she gave Rosalind a bunch of tulips every Friday. After a month the terrier began to wag its tail when Rosalind came. Now it carries the letters to the door in its mouth.
qs: When did the florist give Rosalind tulips?
What does the terrier carry now?
What did the florist give Rosalind?

stories.text: A pair of swallows built a nest under the eaves of an inn. The innkeeper's son wanted to knock it down, but the innkeeper said the birds brought luck. That summer the swallows ate the mosquitoes that bothered the guests, and the inn was never busier. After a storm, the son himself climbed a ladder to mend the nest.
qs: Where did the swallows build a nest?
Who wanted to knock the nest down?
Why did the innkeeper keep the nest?

stories.text: Aleksander kept a spare key under a flowerpot by his back door. On Monday his neighbour, Fenna, used it to feed his fish and then hung it on her own hook by mistake. On Tuesday the plumber could not get in. Fenna found the key on Wednesday and put it back under the flowerpot.
qs: Where was the key at first?
Who used the key on Monday?
Where was the key on Tuesday?
Who had the key after Monday?

stories.text: Captain Reyes flew small planes between the islands. During a delivery of medicine, a seagull struck her windscreen and cracked it. She landed safely on a sandbar, and children from the nearest village rowed out with tape and a blanket. The medicine reached the clinic that evening, only three hours late.
qs: Who rowed out to the plane?

stories.text: A snail wanted to see the top of the garden wall. Each day he climbed a little, and each night the dew washed him back down. A ladybird laughed at him, but a kind caterpillar told him to rest in the cracks at night. By midsummer the snail had reached the top and could see the whole valley.
qs: What did the snail want to see?
the top of the garden wall
What washed the snail back down?
Who told the snail to rest in the cracks?
When did the snail reach the top?

stories.text: At nine the bride's ring was in a velvet box on the hotel dresser. The best man, Callum, slipped it into his jacket pocket before driving to the church. During the photographs he hung the jacket on a gate, and a goat began to chew the sleeve. The ring was still in the pocket when the vicar asked for it at eleven.
qs: Where was the ring at nine?
Who had the ring before the church?
Where did Callum hang his jacket?

stories.text: Every Sunday a widower named Lorcan sold honey cakes at the harbour market. A rival stall, run by two brothers, sold the same cakes for less. Lorcan began telling a story aloud to the people waiting in his queue. Soon his queue was longer than theirs, even though his cakes cost more.

Every morning the baker, Teodor, opened his shop on Quay Lane at six. On Thursday his oven would not light, so he called his cousin Radu, who fixed gas pipes for a living. While Radu worked, Teodor sold yesterday's bread at half price. By noon the oven was hot again and the street smelled of rye.
qs: Who did Teodor call when the oven would not light?
What did Teodor sell while Radu worked?
When was the oven hot again?

stories.text: A crow found a ring in the grass and carried it to the top of an oak. A squirrel who lived below asked to see it. The crow, proud of her prize, opened her beak to answer, and the ring fell into the squirrel's paws. The squirrel buried it under the roots, and the crow never found it again.
qs: Who asked to see the ring?
Who had the ring at the end?
Where was the ring at the end?

stories.text: At eight o'clock Wanjiru packed a basket of mangoes and took the bus to the market in town. She sold half of them before lunch. In the afternoon she carried the rest to her aunt's house by the lake, and her aunt made jam with them. Wanjiru slept there that night and went home in the morning.
qs: When did Wanjiru pack the basket?
Where were the rest of the mangoes in the afternoon?
Who made jam with the mangoes?

stories.text: Mrs Adebayo ran the lending library in the village hall. One rainy Saturday a boy named Kazuo returned a book with a torn cover. Instead of scolding him, she showed him how to mend it with tape and card. Now Kazuo helps her repair books after school.
qs: Who returned a book with a torn cover?
What did Mrs Adebayo use to mend the book?
What does Kazuo do after school?

stories.text: A goat wanted the apples on the farmer's tree, but the branches were too high. She asked the horse to shake the trunk, and he did, because she promised him half. When the apples fell, the goat ate every one and left only the cores. The horse never helped the goat again.
qs: Why did the horse shake the trunk?

stories.text: Before breakfast, Dmitri hung his wet boots on the fence. His sister Jovana moved them into the barn when it started to rain. At noon their father wanted to go fishing and took the boots from the barn to the river. That evening Dmitri found them drying beside the stove.
qs: Where were the boots before breakfast?
Who moved the boots into the barn?
Who took the boots to the river?
Where were the boots that evening?
When did their father take the boots?

stories.text: The new nurse at the clinic, Fatou, noticed that an old man in the waiting room was shivering. She brought him a blanket and a cup of tea. The man, Mr Okonjo, said he had walked from the hills because his bus had broken down. Dr Lindgren saw him first, and Fatou drove him home after her shift.
qs: Who was shivering in the waiting room?
What did Fatou bring along with the blanket?
Why had Mr Okonjo walked from the hills?

stories.text: A young owl could not sleep during the day because a woodpecker kept drumming on her tree. She flew to the wise heron and asked for advice. The heron told her to sleep in the old chimney of the empty mill. There the owl slept soundly, and the woodpecker drummed for no one.
qs: What kept drumming on the owl's tree?
Who did the owl ask for advice?
Where did the owl sleep in the end?
When could the owl not sleep?
What did the owl do in the chimney?

stories.text: On the first day of the trip, Priya and her brother Ravi flew from Delhi to Lisbon. They spent the second day in Porto, where Ravi lost his hat on a tram. On the third day they took a train back to Lisbon, and the hat was waiting for them at the hotel desk, because a driver had found it.
qs: When did Ravi lose his hat?
Where were they on the second day?
Where was the hat on the third day?

stories.text: When the storm took the roof off the school, the headmistress, Ms Mbatha, asked parents for help. A carpenter, Goran, brought timber from his yard. Ten fathers and mothers spent the weekend nailing it in place, and the children had lessons in the church hall until the roof was finished.
qs: What took the roof off the school?
Where did the children have lessons?
How many parents spent the weekend nailing?

stories.text: A fox told a rooster that all the animals had made peace and invited him down from the wall. The rooster said he could see two dogs running toward them and asked whether the fox would wait to greet them. The fox ran off at once. The rooster laughed, because there were no dogs at all.
qs: What did the rooster say he could see?
What had all the animals made, according to the fox?

stories.text: Hamid left his phone on the kitchen table when he went to work. His daughter Yusra found it and put it in her school bag by mistake. At lunchtime she called him from it, laughing, and that evening she handed it back to him at the bus stop.
qs: Where was the phone when Hamid went to work?
What did Yusra put the phone in?
Who had the phone at the end?
When did Yusra hand the phone back?

stories.text: Zeynep, a taxi driver in a busy port city, found a violin on her back seat one night. She drove to the concert hall because the case had a ticket stub inside. The orchestra's cellist, Oskar, had left it there after his last ride. He gave Zeynep two seats for the Sunday show.
qs: Who had left the violin in the taxi?
What was inside the violin case?

stories.text: A mouse fell into a bucket of milk at the dairy. She could not climb the smooth sides, so she kept swimming in circles all night. By morning her kicking had churned the milk into butter, and she stepped onto it and jumped out. The dairymaid found tiny footprints in the butter and wondered what had happened.
qs: What turned the milk into butter?
When did the mouse jump out?
What did the dairymaid find in the butter?

stories.text: The school bus left the depot at seven and stopped first at the farm, where the twins, Malik and Noor, got on. Next it picked up Siobhan at the bakery corner. Malik left his lunchbox on the seat when they reached the school. The driver, Mrs Halloran, carried it back to the depot at the end of the day.
qs: When did the bus leave the depot?
Who got on at the bakery corner?
Who left a lunchbox on the seat?
Where was the lunchbox at the end of the day?

stories.text: Vikram sold umbrellas outside the train station, but it had not rained for a month. One afternoon he started selling cold lemonade instead, and a queue formed at once. Then, while he was pouring the last glass, dark clouds rolled in, and he quickly brought the umbrellas back out.
qs: What did Vikram do when the clouds came?

stories.text: A bear and a badger found a beehive in a hollow log. The bear said he would break it open if the badger kept watch for the bees. The badger watched, but the bear ate all the honey himself. That night the bees found the bear asleep and stung his nose.
qs: Where did the bear and the badger find the beehive?
When did the bees find the bear?

stories.text: Lerato borrowed a ladder from her neighbour Bashir on Monday to clean her gutters. On Tuesday her son took the ladder to the school to help paint a mural. It stayed there until Friday, when the caretaker brought it back to Lerato's garden, and she returned it to Bashir that weekend.
qs: Where was the ladder on Wednesday?
Who took the ladder to the school?
Who brought the ladder back on Friday?
Who had the ladder at the end?

stories.text: The ferry to the island was cancelled because of high winds, so the postman, Sefa, hired a fishing boat. Its owner, an old woman called Akosua, steered through the waves while Sefa held the mail bags. They reached the island before dark, and the islanders cheered when the letters arrived.
qs: When did they reach the island?

stories.text: A peacock laughed at a crane for her plain grey feathers. The crane said nothing and spread her wings. She flew high over the hills while the peacock, with all his bright colours, could only walk in the farmyard.
qs: What colour were the crane's feathers?
What did the crane do after the peacock laughed?

stories.text: At nine the tour group gathered in the hotel lobby, where their guide, Paulo, handed each person a map. They walked to the cathedral and then to the old harbour. At the harbour Tamsin dropped her map into the water. Paulo gave her his own map, and he led the group back to the hotel without one.
qs: Where did the group gather at nine?
Who dropped a map into the water?
Who had Paulo's map after the harbour?
What did Paulo hand each person?

stories.text: Captain Moreau's fishing boat came back empty for the third day in a row. Her crew wanted to give up, but the cook, Idris, suggested they try the cold water past the lighthouse. They found a huge shoal of herring there, and the market in the harbour paid them twice the usual price.
qs: Who suggested trying past the lighthouse?
What did they find past the lighthouse?
What did the market pay them?

stories.text: A lazy cat lived in a grocer's shop and was supposed to catch mice. Instead she slept on the flour sacks all day. One night the mice chewed through every sack, and the grocer put the cat out in the street. After that she caught mice in the alley just to eat.
qs: Where did the cat live at first?
What was the cat supposed to catch?
Where did the cat catch mice at the end?

stories.text: Early on Sunday, Elif took her grandmother's clock from their flat to a repair shop on Bridge Street. The repairman, Mr Varela, kept it for a week. On the following Sunday Elif's uncle collected it and carried it to the grandmother's cottage in the country, where it still hangs above the fireplace.
qs: What did Elif take to the repair shop?
Who kept the clock for a week?

stories.text: Because the lift was broken, Mr Dlamini carried his neighbour's groceries up nine flights of stairs. The neighbour, a retired teacher named Ottilie, invited him in for soup. They talked for hours, and she discovered that she had once taught his mother.
qs: Why did Mr Dlamini carry the groceries up the stairs?
What did Mr Dlamini carry up the stairs?
What did Ottilie invite him in for?

stories.text: A donkey carrying salt slipped in a river, and his load grew lighter as the salt melted. The next day, loaded with sponges, he lay down in the river on purpose. The sponges soaked up the water, and the donkey could hardly walk home.
qs: What did the donkey carry the first day?
What did the donkey do the next day?

stories.text: In the morning the red kite was in Hana's garden, tangled in the plum tree. Her friend Cosmin climbed up and freed it. They flew it on the hill behind the church all afternoon until the string snapped, and the wind carried the kite into the farmer's pond.
qs: Where was the kite in the morning?
What carried the kite into the pond?
Where was the kite at the end?

stories.text: Gulnara, a young chemist, had worked at the paint factory for a month when she noticed a leak in a pipe. She told the foreman, but he ignored her. So she shut the valve herself and wrote to the manager, Mr Ashworth, who promoted her the following week.
qs: What did Gulnara do after the foreman ignored her?

stories.text: Two goats met on a narrow bridge over a deep gorge. Neither would step back, so they butted heads until both fell into the water. Further down the valley, two other goats met on a bridge just as narrow. One knelt down, the other stepped carefully over her back, and both crossed safely.
qs: Where did the first two goats meet?
What did the first two goats do?
What did the first two goats fall into?
What did one of the other goats do?
What did the other goat step over?

stories.text: Umar parked his van outside the bakery at dawn and loaded forty loaves. By eight he had delivered them to the hospital kitchen, and he drove on to the harbour to collect fish for the hotel. While he was at the harbour, a gull stole a sardine from the open crate. At ten the van was back at the hotel, and the chef counted one fish short.
qs: Where was the van at dawn?
Who delivered the loaves to the hospital kitchen?
How many loaves did Umar load?
What did Umar collect at the harbour?

stories.text: The village choir had no piano, so its leader, Orla, wrote to a radio station. A listener in the city, Mr Castellanos, offered his late wife's piano for free. Six farmers drove it up the mountain road on a hay cart, and the choir sang at the spring festival.
qs: What did the choir not have?
Who drove the piano up the mountain road?

stories.text: A sparrow warned the other birds that a farmer was sowing flax, which would one day become nets. The birds laughed and kept eating the seeds. The sparrow went to live near the houses, and when the nets were made, the birds who had laughed were caught in them.
qs: Where did the sparrow go to live?
What did the birds keep eating?

stories.text: At half past six the night guard, Wiremu, locked the museum's golden mask in the safe. At midnight he heard a noise in the east hall, but it was only a cat. In the morning the director, Dr Sandoval, moved the mask from the safe to a glass case in the main gallery for the new exhibition.
qs: Where was the mask at midnight?
Who locked the mask in the safe?
What made the noise in the east hall?
Who moved the mask in the morning?
Where was the mask at the end?

stories.text: After the flood, the farmer Svetlana found that her cows had wandered three miles downstream. A boy from the next village, Yaw, had kept them in his father's barn overnight. Svetlana paid him with a wheel of cheese, and her cows walked home behind his bicycle.
qs: What did Svetlana pay Yaw with?
How far had the cows wandered?
When did the cows wander downstream?

stories.text: A frog wanted to be as big as the ox in the meadow. She puffed herself up and asked her children if she was big enough. They said no, so she puffed harder and harder until she burst.
qs: Who wanted to be as big as the ox?
What did the frog do to look bigger?
What happened to the frog in the end?

stories.text: On Friday evening Mateus left his bicycle at the swimming pool and walked home with friends. On Saturday his mother drove him back, but a cleaner had already taken the bicycle to the police station. Mateus fetched it from the station that afternoon and rode it to his grandfather's farm.
qs: Where did Mateus leave his bicycle?
Who took the bicycle to the police station?
Who drove Mateus back on Saturday?
What did Mateus leave at the swimming pool?
Where did Mateus ride the bicycle?

stories.text: The weather reporter, Kirra Walsh, was meant to read the forecast at seven, but she was stuck in traffic. The sports presenter, Emil, read it instead while she ran up the stairs. Viewers wrote in to say that Emil's forecast was the funniest they had ever heard.
qs: When was the forecast meant to be read?

stories.text: A hungry wolf found a dog chained in a yard and asked why he looked so well fed. The dog said his master gave him meat every day. When the wolf saw the mark that the chain had worn on the dog's neck, he decided he would rather stay hungry and free, and he went back to the forest.
qs: What had worn a mark on the dog's neck?
Where did the wolf go at the end?

stories.text: At noon Ilona's suitcase was checked in at the airport in Budapest. It was put on the wrong plane and spent the night in Oslo, while Ilona slept in a hotel in Madrid. The next morning an airline clerk, Jun, sent it on to Madrid, and by evening the suitcase was in Ilona's hotel room.
qs: Where was the suitcase at noon?
Where did the suitcase spend the night?
Who sent the suitcase on to Madrid?
When did Jun send the suitcase on?
Where was the suitcase by evening?

stories.text: The librarian's dog, a grey whippet called Smoke, escaped through the back gate on market day. He was seen stealing a sausage from the butcher, Mr Abara, and then running across the square. Two schoolboys, Luca and Magnus, caught him by the fountain and walked him back to the library.

The pharmacist, Darius, closed his counter at one o'clock every day to eat lunch in the park. On Monday a girl named Fumiko came running in just before one because her grandmother needed cough syrup. Darius stayed open ten more minutes and found the bottle on the top shelf. Fumiko thanked him and ran home with it while he locked the door.
qs: Where did Darius find the bottle?
When did Darius usually close his counter?
What did Darius do while Fumiko ran home?

stories.text: A tortoise named Kelo wanted to see the sea, but it was three hills away. He asked a gull to carry him, and the gull said she was too small. Then a goat, who was going to the shore for salt, let Kelo ride on his back. By sunset the tortoise was standing in the cold foam, and the goat was licking the rocks.
qs: Who wanted to see the sea?
What did Kelo ask the gull to do?
Who let Kelo ride on his back?
What was the goat doing by sunset?
Where was the tortoise by sunset?

stories.text: At eight, Liang left the bakery with a crate of rolls and drove to the school. He left half the rolls in the school kitchen and took the rest to the hospital on Birch Road. The hospital cook, Mrs Bello, signed for them at ten. Before noon Liang was back at the bakery, washing the empty crate.
qs: Who left the bakery at eight?
Where did Liang take the rest of the rolls?
Who signed for the rolls at the hospital?
When did Mrs Bello sign for the rolls?
What was Liang washing before noon?

stories.text: Hedda fixed bicycles in a small shed behind her house. One rainy afternoon her neighbour Behrouz brought a bike with a bent wheel, and she told him to come back on Friday. Behrouz's son, Emre, could not wait, so he borrowed his cousin's scooter to get to football practice. On Friday the wheel was straight and Behrouz paid with a jar of honey.
qs: Who brought a bike with a bent wheel?

stories.text: A mouse and a mole shared a burrow under a turnip field. The mouse gathered seeds all summer, while the mole only slept and dug. When winter came, the mouse's store was eaten by beetles, but the mole's deep tunnels were full of worms. The mole shared his worms, and the mouse learned that digging was work too.
qs: Where did the mouse and the mole live?
What did the mouse gather all summer?
What were the mole's tunnels full of?

stories.text: Carmen packed her suitcase on Tuesday night and caught the early train to Lisbon. In Lisbon she left the suitcase at her aunt's flat and walked to the harbour. Her aunt, Beatriz, met her there with two tickets for the ferry. That evening the suitcase was still in the flat, but Carmen and Beatriz were eating fish across the river.
qs: Who packed a suitcase on Tuesday night?
Who met Carmen at the harbour?
What did Beatriz have for the ferry?
When did Carmen pack her suitcase?
Where was the suitcase that evening?

stories.text: A water pipe burst under Hollin Street on Saturday morning, and several shops were flooded. The owner of the shoe shop, Kwabena Asante, carried his boxes up to the attic. Firefighters pumped the water out by the afternoon. The street was closed until Monday while the pipe was repaired by city workers.
qs: Where did Kwabena carry his boxes?
What did Kwabena carry up to the attic?

stories.text: A young fox boasted that he could catch the moon in the pond. Every night he jumped into the water, and every night the moon broke into pieces and floated back together. An old heron watched him from the reeds. At last she told him, 'The moon you want is in the sky, and the one in the pond belongs to the pond.'
qs: Who boasted that he could catch the moon?
What did the fox do every night?
Where did the heron watch from?
What broke into pieces every night?

stories.text: On Sunday morning Gustavo took his grandson Ali to the market to buy a goose. They carried it home in a basket, but at the bridge the goose escaped and ran into the river. Ali waded in after it while his grandfather held the basket. By lunchtime the goose was in the yard, and Ali's shoes were drying by the stove.
qs: Who took Ali to the market?
What did they buy at the market?
What did the goose do at the bridge?
Where were Ali's shoes by lunchtime?

stories.text: Dr Ifeoma Chukwu runs the only clinic in Ebute village. Because the road floods in April, she keeps a canoe tied behind the clinic. Last spring a farmer named Jabu cut his hand while she was away visiting her sister. His wife paddled him across in the doctor's canoe, and Dr Chukwu stitched the hand when she returned that night.
qs: Where does she keep a canoe?
Why does Dr Chukwu keep a canoe?
When did Dr Chukwu stitch the hand?

stories.text: A crow and a pig both wanted the last apple on the tree. The pig shook the trunk, but the apple held fast. The crow pecked the stem until it snapped, and the apple dropped into the mud beside the pig. The pig ate it in one bite, and the crow learned to pick her partners more carefully.
qs: What did the crow and the pig both want?

stories.text: The red kettle sat on the stove in Amira's kitchen until noon. At noon her brother Farid took it to the garden to fill the bird bath. He forgot it there, and in the evening Amira found it under the plum tree full of rainwater. She carried it back inside and put it on the windowsill to dry.
qs: What did Farid forget in the garden?
Who took the kettle to the garden?
Why did Farid take the kettle to the garden?
Who found the kettle in the evening?
Where was the kettle at the end?

stories.text: Every Thursday the librarian, Mr Haruto Abe, reads stories to the children in the back room. This week the projector broke, so a boy named Diego held up the pictures instead. Diego's little sister, Asel, sat in the front row and laughed at every page. After the reading, Mr Abe gave each child a paper bookmark.
qs: What did Mr Abe give each child?

stories.text: A beaver built a dam across a stream, and the frogs below it grumbled that their pool was drying up. The beaver ignored them until a heavy storm came. That night the dam held back the flood, and the frogs' pool was the only one in the valley that did not overflow. In the morning the frogs brought the beaver a bundle of willow sticks.
qs: When did the frogs bring the beaver a gift?
What did the frogs bring the beaver?

stories.text: Kamal started his day at the post office, where he picked up forty letters. He delivered most of them on Elm Street before ten. One letter was for a house that had been empty for a year, so he took it back to the post office. Late in the afternoon he cycled to the farm at the end of the valley with a parcel for Mrs Halvorsen.
qs: Where did Kamal deliver most of the letters?
How many letters did Kamal pick up?
Where did Kamal cycle late in the afternoon?

stories.text: Bianca and her husband, Joaquin, opened a small cafe across from the train station. She baked the cakes, and he made the coffee. On their first morning a storm knocked out the power, and the coffee machine stopped. Joaquin boiled water on a camping stove, and the customers drank their coffee by candlelight.
qs: What did Joaquin boil water on?

stories.text: A hen found a shiny button in the yard and believed it was gold. She hid it in her nest and refused to lay eggs, because she was too busy guarding it. The farmer's dog laughed and told her that buttons cannot hatch. Ashamed, the hen dropped the button into the well and went back to laying.
qs: Where did the hen hide the button?
What did the hen do with the button at the end?
Why did the hen refuse to lay eggs?

stories.text: At dawn the ferry left the island with Captain Dora Ferro at the wheel and a cargo of lemons. It reached the mainland port by nine, where the lemons were unloaded into trucks. The captain bought fuel and newspapers and sailed back after lunch. By evening the newspapers were being read in the island's only bar.
qs: Who was at the wheel of the ferry?
When did the ferry reach the mainland port?
When did the captain sail back?
Where were the newspapers by evening?

stories.text: When the school bus broke down on the hill, the driver, Gintaras, phoned the head teacher. The head teacher, Ms Okoro, sent the gym teacher with the school van. The van could carry only nine children, so it made three trips. The last group reached school at half past nine, just in time for the spelling test.
qs: Who was the driver of the school bus?
What did Ms Okoro send the gym teacher with?
What broke down on the hill?
When did the last group reach school?

stories.text: A lazy cat lived in a mill full of mice. Instead of hunting, she made a deal with the mice: they could eat the spilled flour if they kept the rats away. The miller saw no mice in the daytime and praised the cat. But one night he came down with a lamp and found the cat asleep on a sack while the mice swept the floor.
qs: Who made a deal with the mice?
What did the mice have to keep away?

stories.text: Before breakfast Joelle hung the wet sheets on the line behind the guesthouse. At eleven the wind blew one sheet over the fence into the sheep field. A shepherd named Anwar brought it back folded over his arm. By three o'clock all the sheets were dry and back on the beds upstairs.
qs: Who hung the sheets on the line?
What blew a sheet over the fence?
When did the sheet blow away?
Where were the sheets by three o'clock?

stories.text: Hakim sells newspapers from a green kiosk outside the cinema. On rainy days his daughter Leila brings him soup in a flask at noon. Last week a film star stopped to buy a paper and left her umbrella on the counter. Hakim kept it behind the kiosk for three days until her driver came to collect it.
qs: What did the film star leave on the counter?
Who came to collect the umbrella?

stories.text: A snail wanted to visit the fair in the next village, which lasted only one day. Knowing she was slow, she set off a whole month early. Along the way a rabbit laughed at her and said he would leave the day before. The rabbit overslept and missed the fair, but the snail arrived on the morning it opened.
qs: Who wanted to visit the fair?
When did the snail set off?
Why did the rabbit miss the fair?

stories.text: On Monday the museum's blue vase was sent from the storeroom to a workshop to be cleaned. The restorer, Dagny, worked on it for two days. On Thursday it was returned to the museum and placed in the glass case by the entrance. A guard named Cyrus checks the case every hour.
qs: What was sent to the workshop?
Where was the vase before Monday?
Where was the vase placed on Thursday?
Who checks the case every hour?

stories.text: Kiri's grandfather was a fisherman, and he taught her to tie knots on the porch. When she was twelve, she entered a sailing race on the lake. Her boat lost its rudder halfway, but she steered with an oar and finished fourth. Her grandfather, who had watched from the jetty, cheered louder than anyone.
qs: Who taught Kiri to tie knots?
How old was Kiri when she entered the race?
Where did her grandfather watch the race from?

stories.text: A bear found a beehive in a hollow log and wanted the honey. The bees stung his nose, so he asked a badger for advice. The badger told him to wait until night, when the bees were asleep. The bear waited, ate the honey in the dark, and woke the next day with a sticky but unstung face.
qs: Who did the bear ask for advice?
What did the bear do after waiting?
When did the bear eat the honey?

stories.text: Elena's map of the old town started the day in her backpack. At the cathedral she gave it to a lost tourist, a man named Florin, who was looking for the river. Florin left the map on a bench by the river when he sat down to eat. In the afternoon a street cleaner picked it up and pinned it to the notice board at the tourist office.
qs: Who had the map after Elena gave it away?
Where did Elena give the map away?
Where did Florin leave the map?
Who picked up the map in the afternoon?
Where was the map at the end?

stories.text: Babajide drives a taxi at night and sleeps until noon. His upstairs neighbour, Mrs Jankowska, practises the piano every morning. Instead of complaining, Babajide bought earplugs, and she started playing only after eleven. Now they share a pot of tea on Sundays.
qs: What does Babajide drive at night?
When does Mrs Jankowska play the piano now?
What do they share on Sundays?

stories.text: A peacock and a sparrow were caught in a net set by a hunter. The peacock spread his tail and screamed, which only tangled him further. The sparrow kept still and slipped through a torn corner. Before the hunter returned, she came back with a mouse, who chewed through the cords and set the peacock free.
qs: What did the peacock do in the net?
Who slipped through a torn corner?
What did the mouse chew through?

stories.text: Leon's school trip began at the zoo, where the class watched the penguins being fed at nine. Then the bus took them to the science museum, and they ate their sandwiches on its steps. At two they visited the planetarium next door. Leon left his cap on the bus, and the driver, Abebe, kept it for him until Monday.
qs: What did the class watch at the zoo?
When did the class visit the planetarium?
Where did Leon leave his cap?
What did the class eat on the museum steps?

stories.text: Aditi runs a stall that repairs phones in the covered market. Her assistant, Collins, is very fast but often loses the small screws. On Wednesday a customer's screw rolled under the stall, and Collins spent an hour looking for it. Aditi found it in the end with a magnet tied to a stick.
qs: Who often loses the small screws?
What did Collins do on Wednesday?
How did Aditi find the screw?

stories.text: A hedgehog and a hare both wanted to sleep in the same dry hollow during a storm. The hare said he was faster and had arrived first, but the hedgehog had slept there for years. An owl suggested they share it, the hare at the front and the hedgehog at the back. By morning the hare was grateful, because the hedgehog's spines had kept a hungry weasel away.
qs: What did the hedgehog and the hare both want to sleep in?

stories.text: Ji-woo's suitcase was checked in at Seoul and should have flown with her to Frankfurt. Instead it was put on a plane to Helsinki by mistake. It reached Frankfurt a day later, where a courier, Hendrik, drove it to her hotel. By then Ji-woo had already bought a new toothbrush.
qs: Where was the suitcase checked in?
Where was the suitcase sent by mistake?
Who drove the suitcase to her hotel?
When did the suitcase reach Frankfurt?

stories.text: The town's oldest baker, Lorenzo, retired this spring after fifty years. His apprentice, Giulietta, took over the shop on Bell Street. On her first day the bread came out flat, because she had forgotten the salt. Lorenzo, who still came by for coffee, tasted it and laughed.
qs: Why did the bread come out flat?
How many years had Lorenzo been a baker?

stories.text: A young owl was afraid of the dark, which is a problem for an owl. Her mother sent her to the glow-worms at the edge of the marsh. The glow-worms lit a path for her every night for a week. By the end of the week the owl was flying alone, and the glow-worms had a friend who kept the frogs from eating them.
qs: Who was afraid of the dark?
Who sent the owl to the glow-worms?
What did the glow-worms do for the owl?
Who did the owl keep from eating the glow-worms?

stories.text: Gabriel and his sister Lidia went fishing on the lake at six in the morning. By eight they had caught nothing, so they rowed to the far shore near the old boathouse. There Lidia caught a trout, and Gabriel caught a boot. They were home by noon, and the trout was cooked for lunch while the boot was hung on the shed.
qs: Where did they row at eight?

stories.text: A lost parrot was returned to its owner in Dunmore on Friday after three weeks away. The bird, called Kiwi, had been living in the bell tower of the church. The bell ringer, Augustin, heard it whistling a pop song and called the local radio station. The owner, a retired nurse, recognised the song at once.
qs: What was returned to its owner?

stories.text: A proud rooster crowed every morning and believed his voice made the sun rise. One day he caught a cold and could not crow at all. He hid in the barn, but when he peeked out the sun was already shining. A goose passing by told him the sun had never needed his help.
qs: Who believed his voice made the sun rise?
Why could the rooster not crow?
Who told the rooster the sun never needed his help?
What was the sun doing when the rooster peeked out?

stories.text: The library's only copy of a cookbook was borrowed by Kasia on the first of May. She lent it to her flatmate Duc, who took it to his parents' house in the country. His mother copied six recipes and posted the book back to the city. It was returned to the library on the twentieth, two days late.
qs: Who borrowed the cookbook from the library?
Who had the cookbook after Kasia lent it?
Where did Duc take the cookbook?
How many recipes did Duc's mother copy?
When was the cookbook returned to the library?

stories.text: Every evening Faisal walks the neighbour's dog, Biscuit, because the neighbour, old Mr Larsen, has a bad knee. Yesterday Biscuit pulled free and chased a cat into the churchyard. Faisal found him tangled in a rosebush and carried him home. Mr Larsen thanked Faisal with a slice of cake.
qs: Who walks the dog every evening?
What did Mr Larsen thank Faisal with?

stories.text: The pharmacist, Oksana, closed her shop early on Friday because her daughter Yara had a school concert. Before leaving, she asked her neighbour Tadeusz to water the plants in the window. Yara played the violin at the concert, and Oksana sat in the front row. Afterwards they bought noodles from a stall near the station.
qs: Why did Oksana close her shop early?
Who did Oksana ask to water the plants?
What did Yara play at the concert?
What did they buy from a stall?

stories.text: A goat and a hedgehog shared a field beside a river. One windy afternoon the goat's bell was blown into the reeds, and she could not reach it with her long legs. The hedgehog, who was small enough to crawl between the stems, fetched the bell and rolled it back to her. 'You may sleep in my shed whenever you like,' said the goat, and from that day the hedgehog slept there every night.
qs: What was blown into the reeds?
Who could not reach the bell?
What did the goat let the hedgehog do?

stories.text: At seven in the morning Rashid loaded a crate of oranges onto his van at the market. He drove the crate to a cafe on Pine Street, where the owner, Sidonie, signed for it. At ten he collected empty bottles from the same cafe and took them to the recycling depot. By lunch the van was parked again outside his flat.
qs: What did Rashid load onto his van?
What did Rashid collect at ten?
Where did Rashid take the bottles?
Where was the van by lunch?

stories.text: Nnamdi repairs bicycles in a garage behind his uncle's bakery. On Monday a girl named Yetunde brought him a bike with a bent wheel. He straightened the wheel, but the brakes were worn too, so he replaced them as well. Yetunde paid him with a loaf from the bakery and a handful of coins.
qs: Who brought Nnamdi a bike with a bent wheel?
When did Yetunde bring the bike?

stories.text: A mole who could not see well opened a small shop that sold spectacles to the other animals. The owl came first and bought a pair, though she did not need them. When the badger asked her why, the owl said that the mole's shop would close if nobody bought anything. Soon the badger and the rabbits bought spectacles too, and the mole's shop stayed open all winter.
qs: What did the mole's shop sell?
Who came to the shop first?
Who asked the owl why she bought spectacles?
How long did the mole's shop stay open?

stories.text: On Saturday Shirin took the early train from Leeds to visit her grandmother in York. She left her umbrella on the train, but a guard named Wilfred handed it in at the lost-property desk at York station. In the afternoon Shirin and her grandmother walked along the city walls. Before going home she picked up the umbrella from the desk.
qs: What did Shirin and her grandmother walk along?
Where did Shirin leave her umbrella?
Where was the umbrella in the afternoon?

stories.text: Firefighters were called to a flat on Mercer Road on Tuesday night after a pan of oil caught fire. The tenant, Tevita Fonua, had gone to answer the door while his supper was cooking. Nobody was hurt, but the kitchen was badly damaged. The fire chief, Ms Szabo, reminded residents never to leave a hot pan alone.

A hungry crane stood on one leg at the edge of a lake and pretended to sleep. A family of frogs swam closer to look at her, but the oldest frog noticed that one of her eyes was open. 'Down, all of you!' he croaked, and the frogs dived under the lily pads. The crane went home with an empty stomach.
qs: What did the oldest frog do?
Who swam closer to look at the crane?

stories.text: The school bus left the depot at half past seven with the driver, Mr Ozturk, and no passengers. It stopped first at the farm gate, where the twins Mateo and Nell climbed aboard. At the bridge it picked up four more children. By eight the bus was outside the school, and Mr Ozturk drove it back to the depot after the bell rang.
qs: Who climbed aboard at the farm gate?
How many children got on at the bridge?
Where was the bus at eight?
When did the bus leave the depot?

stories.text: Zainab teaches swimming at the public pool on weekday evenings. Her youngest pupil, Ruben, was afraid of the deep end for months. One evening, while Zainab held a float for him, he let go and swam the whole length by himself. His father, who was watching from the benches, clapped so loudly that everyone turned to look.
qs: Who was afraid of the deep end?
What did Zainab hold for Ruben?
Where was Ruben's father watching from?

stories.text: A spider spun her web across the doorway of an old barn. Every morning the farmer's broom tore it down, and every night she built it again. One morning a swallow said to her, 'Move up to the rafters, where no broom can reach.' The spider took the advice, and her new web lasted the whole summer.
qs: Where did the spider first spin her web?
Who told the spider to move?
What did the spider do every night?

stories.text: Mina's red kite started the day in the cupboard under the stairs. After breakfast she carried it to the hill behind the church and flew it for an hour. The string snapped, and the kite landed in Mr Quintero's apple tree. He climbed a ladder at noon and brought it down, and by evening it was back in the cupboard.
qs: Where was the kite before breakfast?
When did Mr Quintero bring the kite down?

stories.text: The village library had only one computer, and the librarian, Tamati, kept a list of who could use it each day. On Wednesday a student named Svetla needed it for an essay, but a retired sailor called Teunis had already booked the morning. Teunis offered to swap his slot, so Svetla wrote her essay before lunch and Teunis read the newspapers instead.
qs: What did Svetla need the computer for?
When did Svetla write her essay?

stories.text: A young camel complained that her hump was ugly and asked a lizard to help her hide it. The lizard found a blanket, but under it the camel grew hot and thirsty on the long walk to the oasis. When her mother explained that the hump stored food for long journeys, the camel threw away the blanket. She never complained about her hump again.
qs: What did the young camel complain about?
Who explained what the hump was for?
What did the camel throw away?

stories.text: Early on Sunday, Murat rowed his small boat from the harbour to Gull Island to collect driftwood. The fog came in while he was on the beach, so he waited in a fisherman's hut until it cleared. He rowed back in the late afternoon with the boat full of wood. His sister Selin met him at the harbour wall with a flask of tea.
qs: What did Murat go to collect?
Where did Murat wait for the fog to clear?
Who met Murat at the harbour wall?

stories.text: Siddharth works the night shift as a security guard at the museum. At two in the morning he heard a noise in the stone gallery and went to look with his torch. A pigeon had flown in through a broken window and knocked a small vase off its stand. Siddharth caught the bird in his cap and let it out of the front door.
qs: Who works as a security guard?
Where did Siddharth hear the noise?
What knocked the vase off its stand?
What had the pigeon knocked off its stand?
What did Siddharth catch the pigeon in?

stories.text: A beaver built a dam that made a quiet pool in the stream. The ducks loved the pool, but a heron complained that the fish no longer came to her shallow corner. So the beaver opened a small gap in the dam, and some water ran past the heron's corner again. After that the ducks kept their pool, and the heron caught her fish as before.
qs: What did the beaver open in the dam?
What did the heron catch again?

stories.text: The parcel from Ulrike's aunt left Vienna on Monday and reached the sorting office in Graz on Tuesday. On Wednesday morning the postman, Sandro, put it in his van, but Ulrike was out, so he left it with her neighbour Mrs Pohl. Ulrike collected it from Mrs Pohl that evening and found a woollen scarf inside.
qs: Where did the parcel leave from?
Where was the parcel on Tuesday?
Who had the parcel on Wednesday afternoon?

stories.text: When the rain flooded the road to the clinic, the nurse, Thandiwe, borrowed her brother's tractor to reach her patients. She drove it through the water with her medical bag on the seat beside her. At the first farm she checked on an old man named Opoku, whose leg was healing well. Later she delivered medicine to a mother with a sick baby.
qs: What did Thandiwe deliver to the mother?

stories.text: A magpie collected shiny things and kept them in her nest at the top of a pine. One day she found a spoon and a button on the same path, but she could carry only one. While she was deciding, a jackdaw flew down and took the spoon. 'The button was prettier anyway,' the magpie told herself, and she flew home with it.
qs: Where did the magpie keep shiny things?
What did the magpie take home?
Why could the magpie not take both things?

stories.text: At dawn the shepherd, Zoltan, led his sheep from the barn up to the high meadow. At midday he moved them down to the stream so they could drink. Because a storm was coming, he drove them back into the barn at four and bolted the door. Only one lamb was missing, and his dog found it sheltering under a hedge.
qs: Where did Zoltan lead the sheep at dawn?
Where were the sheep at midday?
What did Zoltan do to the barn door?

stories.text: Rafael and his grandfather spent Saturday painting the garden fence green. Rafael painted the low boards, while his grandfather did the tall posts. A neighbour's cat walked along the top of the fence and left green paw prints on the shed roof. Grandfather laughed and said the cat had signed their work.
qs: What colour did they paint the fence?
What left paw prints on the shed roof?
Where did the cat leave paw prints?

stories.text: Two ants found a grain of rice too heavy for either of them. The red ant pulled it from the front and the black ant pushed from behind, but they kept going in different directions. 'Walk on the same side,' said a beetle who was watching from a leaf. They lifted the grain together and carried it to their hill before dark.
qs: Who was watching from a leaf?
Where did the ants carry the rice?

stories.text: Nyokabi packed her tent and left the city on Thursday to cycle to the lake. She spent the first night at a campsite beside a tea farm. On Friday the road climbed through a forest, and she reached the lake at sunset. She stayed there two nights before riding home by bus with her bicycle on the roof.
qs: Where did Nyokabi spend the first night?
When did Nyokabi reach the lake?
How many nights did she stay at the lake?
When did Nyokabi leave the city?

stories.text: The cook at the hospital, Prakash, had made soup for a hundred people when he learned that the delivery of bread would not arrive. He telephoned a baker named Odile, who sent her son across town with three sacks of rolls. The rolls came just before lunch, and the patients never knew anything had gone wrong.
qs: Who brought the rolls across town?
How many sacks of rolls were sent?

stories.text: A rooster believed that the sun rose because he crowed. One morning he had a sore throat and could not make a sound. He hid in the henhouse, sure that the day would stay dark, but the hens woke him and showed him the bright sky. 'I suppose I will crow just for fun now,' he said.
qs: Who believed the sun rose because he crowed?
Why could the rooster not crow?
What did the hens show him?

stories.text: The museum's oldest painting, a portrait of a sea captain, hung in the main hall until March. Then it was taken down and driven to a workshop in Braga, where a restorer named Marisol cleaned it for six weeks. In May it travelled back by lorry, and now it hangs in a small room near the library.
qs: What is the museum's oldest painting?
Where did the painting hang until March?
Where was the painting in April?
How long did Marisol clean the painting?

stories.text: Every Friday, Saoirse sells honey from her bees at the market square. This week a tourist bought six jars early, so she had only two left by ten o'clock. Her friend Rui, who sells cheese at the next stall, lent her his cool box so she could fetch more honey from her farm. She was back before the church bell rang eleven.
qs: Where does Saoirse sell her honey?
How many jars did the tourist buy?
Who lent Saoirse a cool box?

stories.text: A little fish lived in a bucket that a boy had left on the shore. Each day the boy fed her crumbs, and each day she grew a little bigger. One morning a wave came high up the beach and tipped the bucket over. 'Thank you for the crumbs!' the fish called as she swam out into the sea, and the boy waved goodbye from the rocks.
qs: Where did the little fish live?
What did the boy do from the rocks?

stories.text: Valeria lost her keys on Tuesday. She still had them after breakfast, because she locked the front door with them before walking to the bakery. At the bakery she put them on the counter while she paid for a cake. The baker, Mr Saliba, found them after she left and kept them in the till drawer until she came back at five.
qs: When did Valeria lose her keys?
Where did Valeria put her keys at the bakery?
Where were the keys until five?

stories.text: Yoshiro had been a bus driver for thirty years, and on his last day the passengers surprised him. A schoolgirl named Pia handed him a card that everyone had signed, and an old woman gave him a tin of biscuits. At the final stop he thanked them all through the loudspeaker. His wife, Nobuko, was waiting at the depot with flowers.
qs: What did Yoshiro do at the final stop?
What did the old woman give him?
Who was waiting at the depot?
What did Nobuko have with her at the depot?

stories.text: Every morning a lazy bear knocked on the bees' hive and asked for honey instead of looking for berries. The bees grew tired of him and moved their hive to a hollow too narrow for his paw. When the bear came the next day, he found only an empty branch. That summer he learned which bushes had the sweetest berries.
qs: What did the bear ask the bees for?
Where did the bees move their hive?
What did the bear find the next day?
Why did the bees move their hive?

stories.text: On the first day of the school trip, the class took a ferry from the mainland to the island of Vass. They spent the morning at the lighthouse and ate lunch in the ruined chapel. In the afternoon their teacher, Mrs Quist, led them along the cliffs to a seal colony. They slept that night in a youth hostel near the pier.
qs: What did the class take to the island?
Where did the class spend the morning?
Who led the class along the cliffs?
When did the teacher lead the class along the cliffs?

stories.text: Paloma mends shoes in a narrow shop next to the town hall. On Thursday the mayor, Mr Rautio, brought in a pair of boots with a broken heel. Paloma fixed the heel the same afternoon, and her brother Santiago delivered the boots to the town hall before the evening meeting.
qs: What was wrong with the mayor's boots?
When did Paloma fix the heel?

stories.text: A peacock and a sparrow argued about who was more useful to the garden. The peacock spread his tail and said that visitors came only to admire him. The sparrow said nothing but ate the caterpillars from the gardener's cabbages all afternoon. In the evening the gardener scattered seed for the sparrow and shooed the peacock off the lettuces.
qs: What did the peacock and the sparrow argue about?
Who did the gardener scatter seed for?

stories.text: The ice-cream van belongs to Umberto, and on summer days it follows the same route. It parks by the swimming pool from eleven until one, then moves to the park gates for the afternoon. At five it goes to the beach car park, and at eight Umberto drives it home to his garage on Elm Street.
qs: Where is the van at noon?
Where is the van in the afternoon?
When does the van go to the beach car park?
When does Umberto drive the van home?

stories.text: Milena was elected captain of the school chess team in September. The team lost its first match, so she organised extra practice every Tuesday in the science room. Their coach, Mr Petrov, brought old puzzles from his own collection. By spring the team had won the county cup, and Milena's photo was printed in the local paper.
qs: Who was captain of the chess team?
When did the extra practice take place?

stories.text: A young hare boasted that nobody could jump the brook. A frog said nothing, sat on a stone in the middle, and hopped across in two jumps. The hare tried in one leap, landed in the water, and was carried down to the mill pond. 'Grab this,' called the frog, and he pushed a stick toward her so she could climb onto the bank.
qs: Who boasted that nobody could jump the brook?
What did the hare land in?
How many jumps did the frog need?
What did the frog push toward the hare?

stories.text: The church bell was cracked, so on Monday workers lowered it from the tower onto a cart. The cart took it to a foundry in the next valley, where it was melted and cast again. Three weeks later the new bell came back on the same cart, and the priest, Father Mihai, rang it at the wedding of Sabine and Rolf.
qs: Why was the bell lowered from the tower?
Where did the cart take the bell?
When did the new bell come back?
Whose wedding was the bell rung at?

stories.text: Roswitha and her neighbour Wim share a vegetable plot behind their block of flats. Roswitha grows tomatoes and beans, while Wim prefers potatoes. In August a storm flattened the beans, but Wim's potatoes were safe under the soil. He gave Roswitha a basket of potatoes, and she cooked a stew for them both.
qs: When did the storm flatten the beans?

stories.text: At the small radio station on Gullbrae Hill, the night presenter, Solveig, read the weather at ten. Her producer, Wojciech, had left a note on the desk because the second microphone was broken. Solveig borrowed a headset from the sports room and finished the show with it. When the morning team arrived, they found the note still taped to the desk.
qs: Who had left a note on the desk?
Where did Solveig borrow a headset from?
When did Solveig read the weather?

stories.text: A magpie named Corvo lived above a beekeeper's yard. One spring he wanted honey, but the bees would not let him near the hives. Corvo asked a slow old toad, Bembo, for advice, and the toad told him to bring the bees a gift of clover. The magpie flew to the far meadow and carried back three stems of clover in his beak. After that, the queen bee let him taste one drop of honey each evening.
qs: Who did Corvo ask for advice?
What did the toad tell Corvo to bring the bees?
How many stems of clover did Corvo carry back?
Who let Corvo taste the honey?

stories.text: The ferry left Pellmouth at seven with a crate of lemons on deck. Halfway across, a deckhand named Kodzo moved the crate into the cabin because spray was soaking it. At Dunmere the crate was carried off by a porter, who loaded it onto a mule cart. By noon the lemons were in the market at Dunmere, stacked beside the fish stalls.
qs: Where was the crate of lemons when the ferry left?
Who moved the crate into the cabin?
Why did Kodzo move the crate?
Who carried the crate off the ferry?
Where were the lemons by noon?

stories.text: Mrs Olatunji ran a tailor's shop on Kettle Street, and her apprentice, Florian, swept the floor each morning. On Monday a customer brought in a torn wedding jacket. Florian wanted to mend it himself, but Mrs Olatunji said the silk was too fine for a beginner. She sewed the sleeve while he pressed the trousers, and the jacket was ready by Wednesday.
qs: Who swept the floor each morning?
What did the customer bring in?
What did Florian do while Mrs Olatunji sewed the sleeve?

stories.text: In a dry valley, a hedgehog named Pim found a puddle after the storm. A proud crow landed beside it and said the water belonged to whoever saw it first. Pim pointed out that he had been drinking before the crow arrived. Just then a fox trotted up and drank half the puddle while they argued. The hedgehog and the crow shared what was left and never quarrelled about water again.
qs: What did Pim find after the storm?
Who said the water belonged to whoever saw it first?
When did Pim find the puddle?
What did the hedgehog and the crow do with what was left?

stories.text: At dawn the pickers met at the top of the Lessard vineyard. Their baskets were stacked by the stone wall, and the foreman, Ruy, handed them out. By eleven the baskets were full, so a tractor took them down to the press house. In the afternoon Ruy's daughter Ghislaine counted the grapes at the press house and wrote the total in a red book.
qs: Where did the pickers meet at dawn?
What took the baskets down to the press house?

stories.text: Every Friday a night market opens in the car park behind the library. Mei sells dumplings there from a blue stall, and her neighbour, an old man called Faruk, sells lamps. Last Friday the wind blew one of Faruk's lamps off his table. Mei caught it before it hit the ground, and Faruk gave her a small lamp to thank her.
qs: Where does the night market open?
What blew a lamp off Faruk's table?

stories.text: A young goat, Brisa, wanted to cross the river to eat the tall grass on the other side. The otter who lived under the bank offered to carry her on a log if she promised to share. Brisa promised, but on the far side she ate all the grass herself. The next week the river rose, and when Brisa asked for a ride home, the otter only laughed and swam away.
qs: Who wanted to cross the river?
What did the otter offer to carry her on?
What did Brisa do on the far side?

stories.text: Two climbers, Maren and Anselmo, reached the glacier hut late in the afternoon. Maren left her ice axe outside the door, but in the night snow buried it. In the morning the hut warden, a quiet woman named Gudrun, dug the axe out with a shovel. The climbers set off for the summit at six, and Anselmo carried the rope.
qs: Where did Maren leave her ice axe?
What did Gudrun dig the axe out with?

stories.text: The puppet theatre on Quince Row had only one dragon puppet, and it was kept in a trunk under the stage. Before the Saturday show, the puppeteer, Torgny, could not find it. His niece Liesl had borrowed the dragon to show her class, and she brought it back just as the curtain opened. Torgny was so relieved that he let her work the dragon's tail.
qs: Where was the dragon puppet kept?
Why had Liesl borrowed the dragon?
What did Torgny let Liesl work?

stories.text: A field mouse named Tilde stored seeds in an old boot at the edge of the farm. One cold morning a rat came and claimed the boot was his house. Tilde did not argue; she invited the rat in for breakfast instead. While they ate, the farmer's cat walked past, and the rat was glad the boot had a mouse inside to warn him. From then on the two shared the boot through the winter.
qs: Who claimed the boot was his house?
What did Tilde do instead of arguing?
